On Wed, 24 Jun 2026 at 08:05 Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@healthsyte.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for last week's demo — the team was impressed...

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary of what we can do and open questions so procurement has something concrete: 

- SKUs: we split the on-prem product into 3 building blocks — Operator Licenses (per SRE seat), Site Nodes (per physical site / head node), and Consumption Credits (tokens for per-token workloads). For pilots we often anchor on a small Site Node + Operator bundle and provision a monthly consumption allowance.

- Platform fee offset: we can offer a pilot credit that reduces the platform fee by up to 50% for the pilot period. For conversion to production we typically require a commit that surfaces the remaining platform fees; in exchange we can amortize (apply) the unused pilot credit across the first 6 months of production, or we can convert it into a one-time implementation credit.

Open items from our side for procurement to confirm:
1) Length of pilot + estimated monthly tokens
2) Number of seats (SRE / operator licenses) required during pilot
3) Whether HealthSyte can commit to a 24-month conversion window if pilot is successful (this affects the offset size)

I've looped in Marissa (CS lead) to provide a sample pricing matrix and Ben (sales) for legal / term-sheet questions.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov

Alex / Olga — quick draft of a pricing construct attached (price-matrix-privdeploy-v3.xlsx) and a redline-ready term-sheet (redwood-privdeploy-term-sheet-draft-v3.docx). Notes:

- Pilot bundle suggested: 1 site-node (starter), 3 operator licenses, 200k token monthly allowance. Pilot platform fee is 50% off for 3 months.
- Conversion options: if HealthSyte signs a 24-month commitment within 60 days of pilot end, we apply a one-time implementation credit equal to 75% of the unused pilot platform-credit; alternatively, an amortization option spreads the credit across the first 6 invoice cycles.
- Support tiers: Pilot falls under 'Bronze' (basic SLO monitoring + onboarding hours). Production options: Silver (24/7 oncall with 4-hour P1), Gold (SRE shared rota + runbook customization). Pricing delta between Bronze->Silver is roughly 20% of platform fee; Silver->Gold another ~30%.

Ben — can you confirm whether we can soften the 24-month anchor to 18 months for strategic customers if procurement pushes back?

Cheers,

Thanks Olga/Marissa — procurement followed up after reviewing the attachments. A few points from our side: 

1) Platform fee offset: HealthSyte can accept a pilot credit, but we need an explicit conditional trade: 24-month production commit (or higher committed spend) in exchange for a 45% pilot platform fee reduction and a capped implementation credit.
2) Operator licensing: procurement prefers operator-seat licensing to be capped per environment (dev/stage/prod) rather than per-seat to simplify budgeting. Can Redwood map operator licenses into an environment-bound SKU?
3) Escalation / SLO: we need a written SLA for P1/P2 during pilot conversion window and a defined credit ladder for missed SLOs.

We have redlined a few commercial clauses in the attached PDF (see Annex B comments). Please respond with one clean term-sheet that reflects either (A) a 24-month commit with the 45% offset + capped implementation credit, or (B) an 18-month commit with a slightly smaller offset (35%) and no amortization.

Procurement will be the signatory; Samantha will coordinate legal redlines.

Regards,
HealthSyte Procurement
procure@healthsyte.com
